Deterministic security for action-taking AI

AgentShield

Prompt injection is not solved inside the model. Enforce every tool decision outside the model.

The problem

Agents can read untrusted content, select powerful tools, and be manipulated into unauthorized actions. A persuasive prompt must never become a permission.

Models propose.
Policy decides. AgentShield puts a deterministic reference monitor at the tool-call boundary, where privilege can be checked before dispatch.

The eight-step defense pipeline

01NormalizeCanonicalize the requested tool call.
02Pin schemaVerify the tool schema digest.
03Check policyEvaluate Cedar authorization.
04Check labelsEnforce information-flow ceilings.
05Check trifectaRequire subject, capability, and provenance.
06Check approvalTier consequential actions for a human.
07Check revocationReject stale epochs and kill-switch states.
08Dispatch + ledgerExecute only after checks; append tamper-evident evidence.

Security pillars

Least privilege

Capabilities constrain what an agent may request, not what a prompt asks it to do.

Trusted-input labels

Provenance and label lattices prevent untrusted reads from flowing into sensitive egress.

Human approval

High-consequence actions require signed, nonce-bound approval receipts.

Quarantined parsing

Untrusted data is parsed into a fixed schema and cannot grant privilege to the parser.

Revocation

Epoch counters and a kill switch limit blast radius when credentials or sessions are compromised.

Audit integrity

Hash chains, Merkle trees, and signed checkpoints make security decisions verifiable.

Measured, not merely claimed

AgentDojo suitesWorkspace, Slack, travel, and banking measure benign utility, utility under attack, and targeted attack success.
Deterministic local runRepeatable enforcement-core measurement reports utility, attack success, latency, and denial stage without model variance.
Per-pillar ablationDisable Cedar, label lattice, trifecta, or approval tiering to measure each defense's marginal contribution.
Over-defense checkAgentDyn tasks reveal when a benign task is wrongly blocked even if no attack succeeds.
